findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The allowed, start, candidate, distance, best_distance, and best_time names make the fixed-domain search and cyclic objective explicit, while itertools.product expresses repeated digit selection directly without brittle clock-position case analysis.

The Cartesian product enumerates every four-digit display constructible from the input digit set with reuse, and the hour and minute bounds reject exactly the invalid clock readings. Converting each survivor to minutes and taking its modulo-1440 forward difference measures chronological waiting time across midnight. Reinterpreting zero as 1440 excludes the current occurrence but retains the guaranteed same display on the next day, so the minimum positive distance is exactly the requested next time.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 681, Python, and the native nextClosestTime(time) interface. The app-local solve(time) adapter preserves valid zero-padded 24-hour input, unlimited reuse of displayed digits, strictly later cyclic time, midnight wrap, and zero-padded HH:MM output.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065562197 are algorithmically identical: both build the same allowed-digit set, enumerate four positions, filter the same validity bounds, compute the same cyclic distance, treat a zero difference as one day, and format the closest display. Their only structural difference is the required Solution.nextClosestTime wrapper.

The unchanged authored workloads grow the positive cyclic waiting gap from 1 to 72 to 1440 minutes while the protected algorithm remains bounded by at most 4^4 digit arrangements. A fresh real-test run of the exact protected source passed all 11 ordinary correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.00 and a 1.01x largest runtime ratio. An independently written correct minute-by-minute control passed all 14 outputs but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +0.58 and a 46.62x largest runtime ratio, distinguishing fixed enumeration from work proportional to the cyclic gap.

The Approach accurately explains repeated digit generation, clock-validity filtering, positive modular distance, the full-day interpretation of the identical display, and exhaustive minimality. Its O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims correctly reflect the fixed four-position input and 24-hour domain and match the branch manifest.

The legacy document was replaced by a composition anchor and four modular Reference sections. The independent narrative preserves unlimited digit reuse, exact zero-padded format examples, chronological advancement and midnight wrap, both source examples with every explanatory comparison, and all four constraints.

Authenticated live Premium evidence verified the statement structure, unlimited reuse rule, valid and invalid formatting examples, exactly two source examples with explanations, and all four constraints. The modular Reference is bound to source content hash 325eca6c36730f5af5471ce8f4b1b3623b994e56a27127073f4bb3391da55a02 and every composed local section through source_fidelity.json; direct validation returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact inputs, outputs, and complete explanations appear first and in source order; the local 11:11 check was reclassified from an invented sample to a trial.

All ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden midnight, minute-rearrangement, and leading-zero checks were exposed, leaving no correctness behavior concealed in cases.json.

Contract boundaries cover the fixed five-character zero-padded format, minimum display 00:00, maximum hour 23, maximum minute 59, and all one through four distinct-digit counts. Every input is a valid 24-hour time.

Material behavior covers a one-minute answer, same-hour replacement, minute overflow into a later hour, wrap to the following day, a full-day fallback to the identical display, unlimited reuse, leading zeros, minute-digit rearrangement, and rejection of arrangements whose hour or minute is invalid.

Expected results were checked by an independent forward-minute oracle over the complete domain of all 1440 legal input displays. Both the protected app-local function and immutable verified native method agreed with the oracle for every input and with all authored cases and benchmarks.

All 11 ordinary cases are visible. The unchanged 1, 72, and 1440-minute workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 1440x, and make the correct minute-by-minute control fail only the scaling verdict.
